descriptionAdvanced.en: Foshan, located at the heart of the Pearl River Delta in Guangdong Province, is a city distinguished by its rich cultural heritage and industrial prowess. Renowned as the birthplace of Cantonese Opera and martial arts, Foshan is the ancestral home of legendary masters such as Wong Fei-hung and Ip Man. The city boasts a ceramic manufacturing tradition spanning over a millennium, with the Nanfeng Kiln remaining in continuous operation since the Ming Dynasty. Today, Foshan is a global leader in manufacturing, particularly dominant in the household appliances and furniture industries. The city preserves its traditional charm through the Ancestral Temple (Zumiao), a masterpiece of Lingnan architecture that doubles as a vibrant center for lion dance performances. Its close economic integration with neighboring Guangzhou has forged Foshan into a key component of one of the world's largest megacity clusters. Foshan remains an essential hub for anyone seeking to experience the deep cultural roots of Southern China.

en: Foshan is recognized as the cradle of southern Chinese martial arts, including Wing Chun and Hung Gar.
The Nanfeng Kiln was built in 1506 and is the world's oldest ceramic kiln still in use today.
The Ancestral Temple (Zumiao) is dedicated to Beidi, the Northern God and protector of the region.
Foshan accounts for approximately one-third of the global production of household appliances.
The city is a center for the traditional lion dance, designated as national intangible heritage.
Foshan is linked to Guangzhou by the Guangfo Line, China's first intercity subway system.
